d-dusk/d-riders/d-go/d-wide/d-help (and the night look of hook, hook-name, f-normal, loop): wrong time of day. The CPSC IDI puts emergency crews on scene at about 7:20 PM (news: 7:20-7:24 PM), and sunset in Columbus on 26 July is about 8:45 PM EDT, so the ride failed in daylight. Fix: d-dusk -> 'By early evening, the fair was still in full swing in the summer daylight, and the crowds stayed.' (no sunset, no lights coming on); d-riders 'That evening' -> 'At about twenty past seven that evening' or just 'Early that evening'; set phase to day/late afternoon, not night, on d-riders, d-go, d-wide, d-toll, d-help and the hook, hook-name, f-normal and loop places.

d-fail: 'near the bottom of a swing, the arm gave way' is not in any source (IDI: the gondola 'suddenly detached'; news: broke 'mid-swing', the ride 'swinging above its bottom platform'). Fix: 'Then, mid-swing, the arm gave way.' and drop the 'time slows at the bottom of the swing' moment.

Deaths stated more than once (profile: 'Deaths are stated plainly, once'): the toll is in hook ('1 rider was killed, and 7 more were hurt') and again in d-toll. Keep it once, at d-toll. Hook fix: 'Rust hidden inside one steel arm let a gondola tear off a fair ride in Ohio, with riders on board.' and remove the killed/hurt figs and the tolls/dimAt moment from hook.

hook: the cause is stated as the narrator's own finding; the topic's verify list says the cause only in the bulletin's words, and the CPSC drew no conclusion. Attribute it: '...one steel arm, the maker later said, let a gondola tear off...'. f-maker: add what it said, from NBC News: 'The company said tests on the metal showed corrosion had dangerously thinned the beam's wall.'; and its picture invents a gauge reading and a sealed sample bag, while the IDI says the 30 July visit with the maker was non-destructive, by photography and visual observation: show the engineers photographing and looking at the broken arm instead.

f-quote: 'Here is what it said' presents a paraphrase as the bulletin's words. The bulletin (quoted in the CPSC letter) says: 'excessive corrosion inside the gondola support beam . . . can lead to a hazardous wall thickness reduction of the beam and its adjacent joint, causing the beam to fail under normal operation.' Speak and show those exact words, or change f-alert to 'Here is what it warned.' and make f-quote a plain paraphrase with no quote marks. Any on-screen quote in i-cpsc must also be the letter's exact line: 'a visual inspection after the ride is in place would not detect corrosion thinning of internal walls.'

r-papers: 'there were none' goes beyond the report. The IDI says only that the current owner 'was unable to provide any literature, receipts or service records from the previous owner'. Fix: 'When investigators later asked for service records from the ride's first owner, the current owner could not provide any.' Change the 'folder opens: empty' moment to 'a stamp lands: none provided'.

r-crew: 'They had run it for years' and 'longer than anyone' are not sourced. The IDI says the foreman 'has worked on the incident ride for approximately thirteen years', assisted by two operators. Fix: 'Its foreman had worked on this very ride for many years, with two operators beside him.' (or add 13 as a sourced fact from the IDI and use the placeholder).

c-law: 'Ride owners must now inspect for fatigue and corrosion' is too broad. The rule (Ohio Adm. Code 901:9-1-04.1, under Tyler's Law) requires an annual visual fatigue and corrosion review for intermediate rides, towers and roller coasters, with mitigation as a registered professional engineer recommends. Fix: 'Owners of bigger rides must now have a yearly fatigue and corrosion review...' The photographed repairs and the engineer on the advisory board are confirmed by WOSU (signed by Gov. DeWine, 6 Nov 2019).
